patterns.name: EZ Water Fragmentation / Structured Water Collapse
patterns.frontend_language: impaired tissue buffering / neurovascular oscillator instability
symptoms: pain oscillates rather than being constant and localised
allodynia-like sensitivity without structural nerve injury
patterns.mechanism: When EZ water (structured, gel-phase water surrounding fascia, nerves, and mitochondria) fragments into bulk water, the tissue loses its oscillation-damping function. Afferent signals are no longer attenuated — they amplify into self-sustaining oscillators. This is not neural over-firing; it is a phase-transition failure in the tissue matrix.

modalities: slow rhythmic breathing (reduces bulk-water oscillation amplitude)
structured water support (collagen-rich broths, hydration quality)

patterns.name: Visceral Oscillator Instability (Autonomic Dysreflexia / OAB pattern)
triggers: spinal cord injury or neurodegeneration (removes descending inhibitory control)
bladder filling (mechanical fissure of EZ layer)
symptoms: profuse sweating above level of injury
patterns.mechanism: Not simply 'loss of descending inhibitory control.' The EZ water matrix in bladder, bowel, and skin loses its buffering (damping) function as bulk water ratio increases. Afferent input is amplified rather than attenuated → self-sustaining runaway resonance propagates up the sympathetic chain. The bladder is a gravity-dependent dampness reservoir; the bowel a fermentation-driven internal oscillator; the skin may share embryological field coupling with gut (ectoderm-endoderm co-induction).
patterns.CRPS_analogy: Autonomic dysreflexia = CRPS of the bladder-bowel-skin axis; trigger is internal dampness resonance rather than peripheral trauma.

modalities: structured water and mineral support (Mg, K)

herbs.role: phlegm and dampness resolution, vagal oscillation dampening
herbs.notes: Primary for bulk-water dominance in bladder-bowel axis.

sub_patterns.name: SUNCT / SUNA
sub_patterns.clinical_note: needle-like, hundreds per day, minimal autonomic build-up; responds to anticonvulsants not triptans

triggers: nitroglycerin (NO donor, chaotropic to water matrix)
patterns.mechanism: Same core motor as CRPS and autonomic dysreflexia: EZ fragmentation → matrix feedback loss → self-sustaining oscillator. Localised to the closed cranial resonance chamber (meninges, sinuses, cavernous region). Frequency and gate determine which TAC subtype emerges. Hypothalamus is a phase-synchroniser, not a generator.

oxygen_high_flow.mechanism: mitochondrial redox reset + NO oxidation + bulk water amplitude reduction
oxygen_high_flow.notes: 12–15 L/min non-rebreather. Effective in cluster (bulk-water dominant), less in SUNCT (spike-dominant). Not primarily vasoconstrictive.

triptan.mechanism: emergency phase-clamp on trigeminal oscillator; amplitude cut, not cure
triptan.notes: Effective in cluster; limited in SUNCT (wrong gate).

indometacin.mechanism: membrane-matrix tension rapid reset; vascular-meningeal gate reset
indometacin.notes: PH-specific. Cluster: not effective (dampness too deep). May also induce autophagy.

verapamil.mechanism: oscillatory bandwidth narrowing; parasympathetic amplitude dampening; matrix-feedback stabilisation
verapamil.notes: Low-pass filter + stabiliser. Gold standard cluster prophylaxis. Needs time — field recalibration.

lithium.mechanism: global coherence enhancer; EZ water stability increase; circadian phase synchronisation
lithium.notes: Global coherence modulator. Chronic cluster. Slow but deep reset.

cross_batch_links.note: EZ water fragmentation is the shared biophysical substrate for all Batch 1 cluster patterns. The 7 axes represent different anatomical localisation of the same fundamental EZW collapse phenomenon.
Visceral oscillator instability maps to the Deep Autonomic-Vascular axis (DAV) and Midline Interoceptive axis (MIA) from Batch 1. CRPS analogy confirmed across both batches.

Cranial TAC oscillator has shared mechanism with Lateral Autonomic (LAX) and Posterior Sensory (PSA) clusters from Batch 1. All are expressions of the same EZ oscillator in different geometric locations.
